summary.text: Aptitude is the four-step grading of natural talent for opening and filling an aperture, from A grade down to D grade. It fixes how large the primeval sea can grow and how fast essence recovers.

claims.text: Natural talent for becoming a Gu Master is measured on a four-step scale from A grade to D grade.
The grade is not a social title. It is the limit on how much of the aperture the primeval sea can fill, and it sets how fast that essence recovers on its own.
Clan talk and academy teaching name the same ladder talent or primeval talent.

On Qing Mao Mountain, the Awakening Ceremony measures talent by how far a fifteen-year-old walks into the moon orchid flower sea while Hope Gu enter the body. Fang Yuan states the bands used there: below ten steps means no cultivation talent, ten to twenty is D grade, twenty to thirty C grade, thirty to forty B grade, and forty to fifty A grade.
Not everyone has that talent at all. In ordinary talk, five in ten people may qualify; the Gu Yue clan runs higher, about six in ten, because of the first generation clan head’s bloodline.
Outward gifts such as intelligence, memory, or strength can look like high primeval talent and still fail the ceremony. The walk decides the grade.

The academy elder states the sea fill and the ordinary cultivation ceiling for each band. D grade fills about two to three layers of the aperture and tops out between rank one and rank two. C grade fills four to five layers, usually stops at rank two, and only a small lucky share reaches rank three initial stage. B grade fills six to seven layers and can reach rank three, even rank four. A grade fills eight to nine layers and is treated as fit to reach rank five.

Clan expectation talk before and during the ceremony places the same grades on a social ladder: a D grade youth raised for three years becomes a rank one senior Gu Master and clan foundation; a C grade after about two years usually becomes a rank two senior and clan backbone; a B grade is cared for as a future elder and, with six to seven years of training, a rank three Gu Master; an A grade draws the heaviest investment and is projected toward rank four in about ten years, high enough to contest the clan head seat.
Recovery rate tracks the same gap. Higher talent holds more essence and recovers it faster; primeval stones can offset a lower grade by feeding the sea from outside.
Advancement pace talk later puts a C grade youth at roughly twice a B grade and four times an A grade when rising to middle stage on talent alone.

Talent grades sit beside the aperture mechanics on aperture and primeval essence. The ceremony that produces the grade is on Awakening Ceremony. The four steps are A grade, B grade, C grade, and D grade.
